title: World models understated changes in robot policy success across simulated scenes
summary: Seven learned world models understated the reference change in policy success in 400 of 420 comparisons across 60 paired RoboTwin settings. The authors re-estimated success at the paired endpoints with separate reference runs. Comparisons shared settings and some endpoints. The finding concerns the simulated scene pairs.
ai_technology: World models including Ctrl-World and Cosmos-Predict-2.5

source_review.scope: v1 §3 benchmark construction, §4 setup and simulation-boundary comparisons, Figure 11

evidence.tested: Matching compared policy rollouts under selected paired scene variations with re-estimated reference simulator rates.
evidence.unknown: The pairs were selected to characterize transition boundaries. They are not a representative sample of robotics settings or a physical validation of those transitions. The paper does not specify author affiliations.
evidence.ai_role: World models including Ctrl-World and Cosmos-Predict-2.5 generated rollouts for policies evaluated on matched simulated setups.
